headline: Green Mountain Trail Access and Peak Operations
reservation: Killington Resort uses a dynamic reservation system for winter lift tickets, while Gifford Woods State Park requires day-use fees or camping bookings. Hiking on the Long Trail or Appalachian Trail is generally open, but seasonal mud-season closures are common; check the Green Mountain Club for current status.

days.title: Forest Canopy and Mountain Lakes

stops.name: Gifford Woods State Park
stops.detail: Walk through one of Vermont's few remaining old-growth hardwood forests.

stops.name: Kent Pond
stops.detail: Visit for a quiet shoreline break or to observe waterbirds in the shadow of the peaks.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes from RUT; mountain road conditions vary
days.note: Trails may be muddy in spring; stick to gravel paths to prevent erosion.

days.title: Green Mountain Summits

stops.name: Bucklin Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the western slope of Killington Peak for a challenging hike with significant elevation gain.

stops.name: Killington Peak
stops.detail: Reach the summit for 360-degree views of the Adirondacks and White Mountains.

days.driving: Short local drive to trailhead; parking is limited to small roadside lots
days.note: The final summit push is steep and rocky; carry adequate water and navigation.

days.title: Scenic Ridges and Village Stops
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the K-1 Base Area

stops.name: K-1 Scenic Gondola
stops.detail: Ride to the upper ridge for high-altitude views without the full day's hike.

stops.name: Vermont Route 100 North
stops.detail: Drive this scenic corridor toward Pittsfield for classic New England valley landscapes.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for scenic loop; winding roads require focus
days.note: Gondola operations are seasonal and weather-dependent; check resort status daily.

intel.title: Mud Season Closures
intel.text: High-elevation trails typically close during the spring thaw to protect soil. Check the Green Mountain National Forest site for current trail status.

intel.title: Gondola Windows
intel.text: Scenic gondola rides often end earlier than sunset. Confirm the last cabin down to avoid an unplanned hike.

intel.title: Killington Road Services
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are concentrated at the base of Killington Road and in nearby Rutland. Options are sparse once you head deep into the National Forest.

intel.title: Deep Valley Dropouts
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable on the Bucklin Trail and lower-elevation forest notches. Do not rely on streaming maps for mountain navigation.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Popular spots like the Bucklin trailhead fill early on autumn weekends. Have a backup plan at Gifford Woods if parking is unavailable.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle in Rutland, stock up on mountain snacks, and check the latest weather forecast before heading up US-4.
plan.vehicle: A car with good clearance is helpful for trailhead access; check winter rental policies for snow tires or AWD.
plan.goldenHour: Killington Peak offers panoramic views, but check the gondola schedule or prepare for a hike down in low light.
